cues.en: what I mean is not any particular brand of database, I don't mind whether it's relational or no SQL or whatever.

cues.en: I'm more talking about the the general concept of a database as we use it in building applications.

cues.en: So take for example, your stereotypical web application architecture, where you've got some kind of clients,

cues.zh: 你可以叫它后端或随便什么，它会包含某种业务逻辑，
cues.en: which you may call a back end or whatever you like, um that's will include some kind of business logic,

cues.zh: 通常包括访问控制、规则、接收输入、产生输出等等。
cues.en: typically, access control, rules, accepting input, producing output, whatever.

cues.zh: 当它需要存储数据时，通常会跟数据库通信，
cues.en: Um and that then when it needs to store something typically talks to a database,

cues.zh: 如果需要查询什么，就会查询数据库。
cues.en: if it needs to look something up, it'll query a database.

cues.zh: 这些都是非常标准、熟悉的东西。
cues.en: That's that's all very standard familiar stuff.

cues.zh: 我们通常构建这类系统的方式，是让这个应用层、这个后端保持无状态，
cues.en: And the way we typically build those kind of things is that we make this application layer this this back end stateless,

cues.zh: 这有很多优势，意味着你可以并行运行越来越多的后端逻辑进程。
cues.en: um that has a lot of advantages, it means that you can just run more and more processes in parallel of uh of your back end logic.

cues.zh: 而且，呃，如果你需要处理更多请求，比如，你只要多启动几个这样的实例就行。
cues.en: And uh if you need to handle more requests, for example, you can just spin up more of these things.

cues.zh: 而这些实例中的任何一个，都同样有能力处理某个传入请求，
cues.en: And any of those instances is equally well qualified to handle a particular incoming request,

cues.zh: 呃，因为所需的状态都会按每个请求从数据库里查出来。
cues.en: um because any state that's required will be looked up per request from the database.

cues.zh: 这也很适合 HTTP，因为当然，HTTP 是无状态协议，
cues.en: And that kind of works nicely with HTTP as well because of course, HTTP is a stateless protocol,

cues.zh: 呃，所以能直接轮询路由到任意应用服务器实例就很好。
cues.en: uh so it's nice to be able to just root round robin to any application server instance.

cues.zh: 然而，这种方法的大问题是状态总得有地方放，所以状态就得放进数据库。
cues.en: However, the big problem with this approach is the state has to go somewhere, so the state has to go in our database.

cues.zh: 呃，而我们通常使用这些数据库的方式，实际上就是把它当作一种巨大的全局共享可变状态。
cues.en: Um and the way we typically use those databases is then actually as this kind of giant global shared mutable state.

cues.zh: 这正是我们在共享内存并发中多年来一直试图摆脱的那种可怕东西。
cues.en: It's exactly the kind of horrendous thing that in shared memory concurrency we've been trying to get rid of for ages.

cues.en: All of these nice new uh models for building concurrent systems using actors or um go routines or channels and and so on.

cues.en: You hear many talks about them.

cues.zh: 它们都在试图摆脱共享内存并发，那种你得操心加锁的模型，
cues.en: Um they're all trying to get away from shared memory concurrency where you have to worry about locking,

cues.zh: 还有竞态条件、并发修改、死锁以及诸如此类的问题。
cues.en: um race conditions, concurrent modification, deadlocks and all of these sort of problems.

cues.zh: 我们想摆脱这些，但是
cues.en: We're trying to get get away from that, but

cues.zh: 在数据库方面，我们仍然被这个巨大的共享可变状态困住。
cues.en: with databases, we're still stuck with this giant shared mutable state.

cues.zh: 所以值得想一想：如果我们在单进程应用架构里想摆脱它，
cues.en: So it's worth thinking about, you know, if we're trying to get rid of that in our single process application architecture,

cues.zh: 那如果我们在整个系统层面也试着摆脱这种共享可变状态，会发生什么？
cues.en: what would happen if we try to get rid of this shared mutable state on a whole system level as well?

cues.zh: 目前看来，系统仍然那样构建的主要原因似乎只是
cues.en: Um at the moment, it seems kind of that the main reason why the systems are still being built that way is just the

cues.en: uh the momentum behind it that that's the way we've been building them for ages.

cues.en: And we don't really have the tools to do differently.

cues.en: So this is kind of trying to think about what are the other possibilities of building these stateful systems?

cues.zh: 现在，为了试着弄清楚我们可以走哪些路线，
cues.en: Now, in order to try and uh figure out what kind of routes we could take,

cues.zh: 我想看看数据库目前所做的四类不同例子，
cues.en: I'd like to look at four different examples of things that databases currently do

cues.zh: 以及我们用数据库做的事情。
cues.en: and things that we do with databases.

cues.zh: 这四个例子也许能给我们一些提示，告诉我们这类系统可以往哪个方向推进。
cues.en: And those four examples might give us some hints as to the direction in which we could take these sort of systems forward.

cues.zh: 第一个例子是复制。
cues.en: So example number one is replication.

cues.zh: 嗯，你们大概都了解复制的基本概念：就是把数据副本放在多台机器、多个节点上，
cues.en: Um you probably all know about the basics of replication, the idea is that you have um your copy of your data sitting on multiple machines, multiple nodes,

cues.zh: 而数据库的职责就是让它们保持同步。
cues.en: and it's the database's job to keep those in sync.

cues.zh: 一种常见架构是，把写操作发到一个指定节点，可以叫它 master 或 leader，
cues.en: Uh a common architecture is that you make your rights to one designated node, which you could call a master or a leader,

cues.zh: 然后由它负责确保你做的任何写操作都会被复制到其他机器，这些机器可以叫 follower 或 slave。
cues.en: and that one is then in charge of making sure that any rights that you make are then copied over to any uh of the other machines which you might call followers or or slaves.

cues.zh: 这都很常见，很多系统都是这么构建的。
cues.en: And uh that's that's all very familiar, a lot of systems are built that way.

cues.zh: 我们举个例子看看实际会发生什么，假设一个购物车例子。
cues.en: Let's just take an example to think about what actually happens there, so assume a a shopping cart example.

cues.zh: 这里用的是关系型数据模型，但完全不限于关系型。
cues.en: Um this is using a relational data model, but it's not limited to relational at all.

cues.zh: 假设有一张表有三列：客户、产品和数量，也就是某个客户购物车里有多少件某个产品？
cues.en: Um say you have a table with three columns, they are customers, they are products and quantity, so how many of a particular product does a particular customer have in their shopping cart?

cues.zh: 现在假设客户 1、2、3 中的一位改主意了：不再要一个产品 9，而是要三个。
cues.en: And now say that one of the customer 1, 2, 3 changes their mind and instead of wanting one of product 9, 9, 9 they want three.

cues.zh: 于是你向数据库发出这个查询：update……where 某些条件，等等，把数据库状态从 1 改成 3。
cues.en: So you then issue this query to the database saying update uh where some conditions, blah blah, change the state of the database from one to three.

cues.zh: 结果就是，数据库会在合适的位置应用这个变更。
cues.en: And uh the result is then that the database will go and apply that mutation in the appropriate place.

cues.zh: 现在，
cues.en: Now,

cues.zh: 我刚才讲的是复制。
cues.en: I was talking about replication.

cues.zh: 在复制场景下，这意味着什么？
cues.en: What does this mean in a case of replication?

cues.zh: 通常，你会把这个更新查询发给主库，也就是 leader，
cues.en: Well, you you will typically make this update query to your master to your leader,

cues.zh: 然后它会在本地执行并应用这个更新。
cues.en: and it will then locally execute that and apply it.

cues.zh: 而复制发生的方式有好几种。
cues.en: And now there are several different ways how this replication can happen.

cues.zh: 这次写入如何到达其他节点？
cues.en: How does this write get to the other nodes?

cues.zh: 不同数据库的实现方式不同，比如你可以把预写日志传来传去，
cues.en: Um different databases implement this differently, you can like ship the right ahead log around for example,

cues.zh: 有时也会改用逻辑日志。
cues.en: or what sometimes done is use a logical log as well.

cues.zh: 逻辑日志大概长这样：leader 数据库会产生某个事件，
cues.en: And uh the logical log will look something like this, the leader database produces some event,

cues.zh: 大意是：对于某种内部行或元组标识符，这是旧状态，这是你要改成的新状态。
cues.en: which says something like for some kind of internal row or tuple identifier, this is the old state, this is the new state you should change it to.

cues.zh: 这看上去没什么特别，但注意这里发生了什么。
cues.en: Now, this is, you know, it seems kind of nothing special, but actually notice what has happened here.

cues.zh: 上面基本是一条命令式语句：帮我把匹配某些条件的某些行做这个状态变更。
cues.en: You've got at the top, you've got basically an imperative statement saying make this state mutation for me for some rows matching some conditions.

cues.zh: 而下面这个从一台机器复制到另一台机器的事件，其实形式不同，特征也不同。
cues.en: Whereas below this event that's being replicated from one machine to the other actually has a different form, it has a different characteristic.

cues.zh: 它实际表达的是，在某个特定时间点，某个客户决定把某个商品的数量从 1 改成 3。
cues.en: What it's actually saying is at a particular point in time, a certain customer decided to change the product of a the quantity of a certain product from 1 to 3.

cues.zh: 这其实是一个事实，对吧？
cues.en: And this is actually an a fact, you know?

cues.zh: 即使客户后来又把商品从购物车删掉，或再次修改数量，或离开后再也没买，他们在那个时间点做了这次修改这一事实仍然成立。
cues.en: Even if the customer later removes it from their cart again or if they change the quantity again or if they go away and never buy it, the fact that they at this point in time made this modification remains true.

cues.zh: 与命令式修改相比，这是一个不可变事实。
cues.en: This is an immutable fact compared to an imperative modification.

cues.zh: 所以可以看到，数据库内部其实已经在使用这种不可变性的思想。
cues.en: So we can see that internally, databases are actually already using this idea of immutability.

cues.zh: 先记住这一点，我接下来会讲一些完全不同的话题，之后再回到这个想法。
cues.en: Hold that thought for now, I'm going to talk about some completely different things and then come back to this idea later.

cues.zh: 这四件事中我要谈的第二件完全不同，它是二级索引。
cues.en: The second one of these four things I want to talk about is totally different, it's secondary indexing.

cues.zh: 呃，再说一次，大家可能已经熟悉关系数据库里的二级索引，它算是家常便饭。
cues.en: Uh again, you're probably familiar with what a secondary index is in a relational database, it's like the bread and butter.

cues.zh: 假设你有一张表，还是用同一个例子，嗯，如果你想按不同字段查询它，可能就需要不同的索引，才能高效找到匹配的行。
cues.en: You've got some kind of table, use the same example again, um and if you want to query it by different fields, you probably want different indexes in order to be able to find the matching rows efficiently.

cues.zh: 所以你会做的是，呃，运行一些 SQL，比如在 customer ID 列上创建索引，再在 product ID 列上创建一个单独的索引。
cues.en: So what you would do is uh run some SQL uh creating an index for example under customer ID column and a separate index on the product ID column.

cues.zh: 这样在查询时你就可以用其中任意一个索引。
cues.en: So you could use either of those in in a query then.

cues.zh: 比如，你可以查现在哪些客户的购物车里有某个商品。
cues.en: So you could look up for example which customers have a certain product in their shopping cart right now.

cues.zh: 那么数据库会做什么呢？
cues.en: Now what does a database do?

cues.zh: 当你执行其中一条查询时呢？
cues.en: When you run one of these queries?

cues.zh: 嗯，它会遍历，呃，它会遍历整张表，然后创建
cues.en: Well, it will go through uh it will go through the the entire table, and it will create

cues.zh: 为你创建的每个索引生成一份辅助数据结构。
cues.en: an auxiliary data structure for each index that you've created.

cues.zh: 所以每个索引都会有自己独立的数据结构，用某种不同的方式表示基表中的信息。
cues.en: So each index will have this separate data structure which represents the information in the base table in some different way.

cues.zh: 而这个索引通常是某种键值结构，其中的键实际上会
cues.en: And this index is usually some kind of key value like structure where the keys will actually be

cues.zh: 取自你试图建立索引的某一列，用这些值作为索引中的键。
cues.en: taking the values from a particular column uh that you're trying to index, use those as the keys in the index.

cues.zh: 如果你想给不同的列建索引，那么在另一个索引里，你会取另一列的内容，用它们作为该索引的键。
cues.en: Um and if you're wanting to index different columns, well, for the other index, you would take the content of a different column, use that as the keys of the index.

cues.zh: 关键在于，从这张基表到这里的这些视图，
cues.en: The point being of this is that the process of going from this base table to uh to these these views here,

cues.zh: 也就是这些索引，这个过程完全是机械化的。
cues.en: these um indexes is completely mechanical.

cues.zh: 数据库知道该怎么做。
cues.en: The database knows how to do that.

cues.zh: 你只需告诉它、指示它：给我创建一个索引，它就知道该做什么。
cues.en: You simply tell it, you instruct it, create me an index and it knows what to do.

cues.zh: 只要底层表里的数据发生变化，数据库就会自动更新这些索引，让它们保持一致。
cues.en: And whenever the data in the underlying table changes, the database will then automatically update these indexes to be consistent.

cues.zh: 而且它实际上是以事务方式完成的，所以你可以确定
cues.en: And it actually does that in a transactional way, so you can be sure that

cues.zh: 之后任何访问该索引的事务，看到索引里的数据状态，都会和底层表里的状态一致。
cues.en: any subsequent transactions that access the index will see the data in the index in the same state as it is in the underlying table.

cues.zh: 这其实还挺酷的。
cues.en: That's kind of cool actually.

cues.zh: 更酷的是，有些数据库允许你在处理写查询的同时并发做这件事。
cues.en: Um what's even cooler is that some databases let you do this concurrently with processing right queries.

cues.zh: 比如这是 Postgres 的语法，你可以写 create index concurrently。
cues.en: So uh this is a Postgres syntax for example, it will let you say create index concurrently.

cues.zh: 所以如果你有一张大表，创建索引要花好几个小时，那也没问题。
cues.en: So if you're if you've got a huge table and creating the index takes several hours, that's no problem.

cues.zh: 你不必停止对表的写入，应用仍然可以正常运行、处理写入。
cues.en: You don't have to stop rights to your table, your application can still continue running normally processing rights.

cues.zh: 数据库会在内部自行想办法处理，比如它必须扫描整张表
cues.en: And the database somehow internally figures out how to take like it has to scan the entire table

cues.zh: 来构建这个索引，但与此同时，它还在跟踪这个不断变化的目标。
cues.en: to build this index, but at the same time it's tracking this running this moving target.

cues.zh: 最终，当索引构建完成时，它在事务上竟然能与底层数据的当前状态保持一致，尽管在此期间表已经发生了变化。
cues.en: And at the end, when it's finished building the index, it's somehow transactionally consistent with what the underlying data is saying, despite the table having changed in the meantime.

cues.zh: 这还挺酷的。
cues.en: That's rather cool.

cues.zh: 这就是第二点，我之前想讲的内容。
cues.en: That was number two, thing that I was wanting to talk about.

cues.zh: 第三点。
cues.en: Number three.

cues.zh: 第三点不一样，是缓存。
cues.en: And number three is different, it's caching.

cues.zh: 我这里说的是
cues.en: What I'm talking about here is

cues.zh: 那种应用层缓存，通常你会这样遇到：呃，你知道，你做了个应用、Web 应用，它火了起来，
cues.en: the kind of application level caching that you'll get typically as uh, you know, you build some kind of app, web app, it becomes popular,

cues.zh: 你对数据库的访问压力太大，或者它变得太慢，于是你引入一些 Memcached 或 Redis 之类的。
cues.en: you're hitting the database too hard or it's getting too slow, so you introduce some Memcached or some Redis or whatever.

cues.zh: 很多人把这类缓存引入应用的方式，是在应用代码里自己管理缓存。
cues.en: Um and the way uh many people introduce those kind of caches into an application is to actually manage the cache in application code.

cues.zh: 比如说，有请求进入应用时，你会用某个键先查缓存，
cues.en: So you might, for example, uh incoming request comes into the app, using some key, you will first look in your cache,

cues.zh: 它在缓存里吗？
cues.en: is it in the cache?

cues.zh: 不在，如果不在缓存里，那就是一次未命中。
cues.en: No, if it's not in the cache, that's a miss.

cues.zh: 于是你会去查底层数据库，查询完之后，在返回的路上，你把想要的结果写进缓存。
cues.en: So then you will go to the underlying database, query that, on the way back out, you actually write the the result that you want that you would have wanted to see in the cache.

cues.zh: 把它写回缓存，这样下次有人再请求同样的内容时，
cues.en: You write that back into the cache, so that next time around if someone asks for the same thing again,

cues.zh: 就能直接从缓存拿到，而不用再打到数据库。
cues.en: uh they can get it from the cache rather than hitting the database.

cues.zh: 然后你再把它返回给客户端。
cues.en: And then you return it back out to the client.

cues.zh: 这是一个非常常见的模式。
cues.en: So this uh there's a very common pattern.
